comparisons.peer_summary: AMD recognized $186 million of restructuring charges in 2024 due to the implementation of the 2024 Restructuring Plan, which focused on driving efficiencies and aligning resources with growth opportunities in AI and enterprise markets.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD reported significant restructuring charges in fiscal year 2024 driven by specific restructuring plans. Intel's 2024 Restructuring Plan resulted in $2.2 billion in employee severance and benefit charges, alongside significant non-cash impairments. AMD recognized $186 million in restructuring charges for its 2024 Restructuring Plan, which similarly focused on driving efficiencies and aligning resources with growth opportunities in AI and enterprise markets. While the magnitude differed significantly ($2.2B vs $186M), both companies used restructuring charges to execute strategic shifts involving workforce and operational alignment.

sentences.text: Employee severance and benefit arrangements includes net charges relating to the 2024 Restructuring Plan of $2.2 billion in 2024.

Asset impairment charges in 2024 includes non-cash charges associated with the 2024 Restructuring Plan, including $442 million of non-cash impairments of construction-in-progress assets associated with our decision to exit and outsource manufacturing capabilities for certain internal test hardware; and $103 million of non-cash impairments of operating leased assets and related leasehold improvements resulting from real estate consolidations and exits.
We recognized $186 million of restructuring charges in 2024 due to the implementation of a restructuring plan (the 2024 Restructuring Plan).
The 2024 Restructuring Plan was focused on driving efficiencies across the business and aligning resources with our largest growth opportunities in the AI and enterprise markets.

comparisons.peer_summary: Restructuring and other charges recognized in operating expenses were $1,533 million in fiscal year 2024 and $244 million in fiscal year 2023. The 2024 charges primarily consisted of employee termination costs related to cost reduction activities associated with the VMware Merger, while the 2023 charges were primarily non-recurring charges related to IP litigation.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Broadcom reported substantial restructuring and other charges in fiscal year 2024. Intel recognized $2.2 billion in employee severance and benefit charges related to its 2024 Restructuring Plan. Broadcom recognized $1,533 million in restructuring and other charges, which primarily consisted of employee termination costs from cost reduction activities associated with the VMware Merger. Both companies utilized employee separation costs as a primary driver of their 2024 restructuring expenses, though Broadcom's were tied to M&A integration while Intel's were part of a broader business transformation plan.
